properties.name: Every operation that reads a second design (compare, compose, merge, fork_point, pairing, seam coverage, topic compare, chunk take) takes its other designs BY GRAPH_ID, served by the registry over the designs one process holds, and the host passes the set the caller may read
properties.statement:
Every reflow2 operation whose input is more than one design — compare_designs, compose_and_analyse, merge_designs, fork_point, pair_designs, seam_coverage, and the compare-on-one-topic, seam-gaps and chunk-take operations already accepted — SHALL accept its other design(s) by graph_id as well as by path. By graph_id the registry (cap:graph-registry) resolves each to the DesignGraph the process already holds, opening on demand as it does for a single design, so a hosted server can serve the whole family where today it withholds every by-path tool. The host SHALL pass the set of graph_ids the caller may read on every such call; a graph_id outside that set is left out of the result and the reply says it was left out, never what it held. An operation that WRITES to a second design takes its write locks in one fixed order or refuses, so two cross-design writes cannot deadlock the registry. The result returned is the difference, the candidates or the assembled analysis — never a second design's contents for the agent to diff itself. ORDER OF BUILD (kept as the first step): compare_designs and compose_and_analyse first, measured on flo2.io's registry (open cost once, scan cost per call) before the rest of the family is widened. Settled in dec:idea-cross-design-operations-are-a-primitive-layer-served-by-the-registry-by-graph-id, option (a); its pushback stands: key equality is not design equality across vocabularies, so the cross-vocabulary half remains similarity scoring returning candidates for a judgement. ═══ THE BUILD PLAN, mapped 2026-10-10 at f792e88dc (read-only survey; not started) ═══
TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE WORDING ABOVE. (1) compose_and_analyse does not take a path: ComposeReq { design: JsonObject (an inline export), namespace } (service.rs:5370-5377, tool exchange.rs:1019-1030); the core DesignGraph::compose_and_analyse(&self, other: &GraphExport, namespace) (compose.rs:117-121) builds a throwaway in-memory graph. (2) reflow2 withholds nothing: the flo2 gateway does (engine-door.ts:38-56 REFUSED_TOOLS lists compare_designs at :43; compose_and_analyse is served because its input is inline). A bare --registry-root server with no gateway reads any host path given to compare_designs (read_export_document, service.rs:1678-1680) — a hole to close in the same change.
· WHERE THE DESIGNS ARE: GraphRouter { inner: Arc<Inner> } (registry_http.rs:250-253); Inner.open: tokio Mutex<HashMap<graph_id, Arc<Slot>>> (:238); OpenDesign { http, sessions, store: Weak<RwLock<DesignGraph>> } (:166-174); only the http service closure holds the strong store reference (:630-631). service_for(graph_id) (:466, private) refuses / \ .. and hands back an InFlight guard (:211-223) that keeps the design open for the request. open_design (:560) spawns ReflowService::new_reporting then .without_tree().without_reaching_out().with_caller_rule(..) (:598-621). Eviction: idle sweep (:306-322); LRU close at max_open (:499-512, :642-647); Busy 503 when every slot is in flight (:500-507).
· A TOOL'S self CANNOT REACH THE REGISTRY TODAY: no ReflowService field points to it (service.rs:294-432), and Binding "offers NO way to name a second design. That absence is the isolation property, not an oversight" (registry.rs:191-193).
· BOTH CORE FUNCTIONS NEED ONLY A GraphExport (compare.rs:248-253; compose.rs:117-121), so the core does not change. compare_designs with no other_path already compares the live graph against a base export (compare.rs:481-488).
· LOCKING: SharedGraph(Arc<tokio RwLock<DesignGraph>>) per store (service/unit.rs:163); a write holds write_lock (service.rs:7103, unit.rs:194-210) from the call's first write to its end. Tokio's RwLock lets a queued writer block new readers, so A→B against B→A with writers queued deadlocks: EXPORT THE OTHER DESIGN UNDER ITS READ GUARD, DROP THE GUARD, THEN READ YOUR OWN. Never hold two.
· IDENTITY: reflow2 reads _meta["reflow2/writes_for"] and ["reflow2/acting_agent"] and a bearer VerifiedCaller (service.rs:465-472, 7938-7956; caller.rs:46-48, 128-144). The gateway sends _meta ONLY ON WRITES (engine-api.ts:184-225, reflow2-client.ts:174). A read-only compare carries no identity today, and nothing anywhere says which graph_ids a caller may read.
STEPS, SMALLEST FIRST: (1) a Weak registry handle on ReflowService (Weak, because a strong one cycles Inner→open→Slot→OpenDesign.http→closure→svc→Inner); None in wrap_at (service.rs:6748-6777), copied in share() (:6988-7036), set in open_design beside with_caller_rule. (2) GraphRouter::export_of(graph_id) -> Result<GraphExport, Refusal> on service_for + store.upgrade(), guard dropped before return, InFlight held. (3) a shared resolver ReflowService::other_design(id, &ctx): refuse without a registry ("served only by a registry server; pass a path here"), refuse the design's own graph_id, authorise on CallerRule::TrustedGateway or BearerToken PLUS a new _meta["reflow2/readable_graph_ids"] containing id. (4) compare_designs: ctx + other_graph_id: Option<String>; base_path becomes optional (the surface test forbids only new REQUIRED fields, tests/the_mcp_surface_only_grows.rs:19); refused together with other_path. (5) compose_and_analyse: design optional + other_graph_id, exactly one; namespace defaults to the other graph_id. (6) flo2 gateway: compare_designs out of REFUSED_TOOLS with REFUSED_ARGUMENTS ['base_path','other_path']; membership check on other_graph_id via access.ts; readable-ids _meta on reads as well as writes; regenerate engine-tools.ts. (7) tests on tests/two_designs_stay_apart_over_the_transport.rs's start_registry (:123): allowed, not listed, not on a registry server.
HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, for the owner before any build: (i) IT REVERSES A SETTLED DECISION — registry_http.rs:19-25 "Isolation is a property of WHAT IS THERE, not of a check on who is asking", and dec:the-registry-root-is-the-tenant-boundary refuses filtered listing because reflow2 has no identity system; on flo2 all tenants share one root (engine-api.ts:11-12). Step (3) is exactly such a check; without it any member of design A could read any design on the droplet. A decision reopening that boundary must be recorded first. (ii) Capacity: the second design takes a slot, may evict an idle one or return Busy; at --registry-max-open 1 it is always Busy; a cold open is seconds. (iii) Memory: compose exports both and builds a third graph; real exports run 9-16 MB (reply_budget.rs:19). (iv) No precedent: send_to_design/receive_from_design deliberately make two calls, one per design (flowdown.rs:17-18); this is the first tool that reaches into a second design.
